note: Clubs, sports and indoor games. `name` is the full name used on the catalogue poster; `short` is the label used on smaller cards. Each activity makes a spotlight, fun fact, quiz and quiz-answer flyer. `outfit`, `scene` and `place` build the AI photo prompt shown in the studio.

activities.name: Robotics & Coding
activities.tagline: Build it. Code it. Make it move.
activities.summary: Students design, build and program robots, learning coding, electronics and problem-solving by making things that really work.
doing: Building robots from kits and parts
Coding with block and text languages
activities.fact: The word “robot” was first used in Karel Čapek’s 1920 play R.U.R. It comes from the Czech word robota, meaning forced labour.

quiz.q: What does a sensor do on a robot?
options: Detects things around it, like light or distance
quiz.explain: Sensors give a robot information about its surroundings, so its program can react.

activities.scene: two students building and programming a small wheeled robot on a desk, one typing on a laptop, the other adjusting the robot's sensor

activities.name: Music & Dance
activities.summary: Singing, instruments and dance in traditional and modern styles, building confidence and teamwork on stage.
activities.fact: Zimbabwe’s Mbende Jerusarema dance is on UNESCO’s list of the world’s Intangible Cultural Heritage.

quiz.q: Which traditional Zimbabwean instrument is played by plucking metal keys?
quiz.explain: The mbira has metal keys plucked with the thumbs. Hosho are shakers and ngoma is a drum.

activities.scene: students dancing energetically while classmates play marimba and drums

activities.name: Debate & Public Speaking
activities.summary: Students learn to research, argue and speak with confidence, skills that help in interviews, exams and leadership.
activities.fact: In competitive debate you may be told to argue the side you disagree with. It trains you to understand both sides of an argument.

quiz.q: In a debate, the team that argues for the motion is called the…
quiz.explain: The proposition argues for the motion; the opposition argues against it.

activities.scene: a confident student speaking at a wooden podium while classmates listen and take notes
activities.place: in a classroom set up for a debate

activities.name: Mandarin Connect (Chinese Language for Beginners)
activities.tagline: Nǐ hǎo! Say hello to Mandarin.
activities.summary: A friendly first step into Mandarin Chinese, the world’s most spoken first language: greetings, numbers, pinyin and writing your first characters.
activities.fact: Mandarin is a tonal language: mā (mother) and mǎ (horse) are different words, told apart only by the tone of your voice.

quiz.q: What does “nǐ hǎo” mean in Mandarin?
quiz.explain: Nǐ hǎo is the everyday Mandarin greeting, “hello”.

activities.scene: students learning to write Chinese characters on a whiteboard, one student writing with a marker while others copy into notebooks

activities.name: Le Club Français (French Club)
activities.summary: Conversational French through songs, games and role-play, opening doors to the many French-speaking countries in Africa and beyond.
activities.fact: French is an official language in 29 countries, and more than half of them are in Africa.

quiz.q: How do you say “thank you” in French?
quiz.explain: Merci means thank you. Bonjour is hello and au revoir is goodbye.

activities.scene: students practising a French conversation in pairs, with French books and a small French flag on the desk

activities.name: Cake Making
activities.tagline: Bake it. Decorate it. Share it.
activities.summary: Students learn baking science and cake decorating, from measuring and mixing to icing, piping and presenting a celebration cake.
activities.fact: Baking powder makes a cake rise by releasing carbon dioxide gas when it gets wet and warm.

quiz.q: Which gas makes a cake rise when baking powder reacts?
quiz.explain: Bubbles of carbon dioxide get trapped in the batter and make it rise.

activities.scene: students piping icing onto a tall celebration cake, smiling and concentrating
activities.place: in a clean food technology kitchen

activities.name: Event Décor & Interior Décor
activities.summary: Students plan and style events and rooms: colour, fabric, flowers, lighting and layout, the skills behind weddings, parties and beautiful homes.
activities.fact: Colours opposite each other on the colour wheel, like blue and orange, are called complementary. Used together, they make each other look brighter.

quiz.q: Which colour is complementary to blue?
quiz.explain: Orange sits opposite blue on the colour wheel.

activities.scene: students styling an elegant event table with navy and gold linen, flowers and candles
activities.place: in the school hall decorated for an event

activities.name: Welding & Aluminium Fabrication
activities.summary: Hands-on workshop training in cutting, shaping and joining metal and aluminium to make frames, gates and furniture, with safety first.
activities.fact: Aluminium is the most common metal in the Earth’s crust, yet it was once so hard to extract that it was worth more than silver.

quiz.q: Why must a welder wear a dark helmet?
options: To protect the eyes from intense light and sparks
quiz.explain: A welding arc gives off intense light that can damage the eyes, so the helmet filters it.

activities.scene: a student welding a metal frame with sparks flying safely while an instructor watches

activities.name: Beauty Therapy (Pedicure & Manicure)
activities.summary: Professional nail care, manicure and pedicure, hygiene and client care: the first steps towards a career in the beauty industry.
doing: Client care and running a small business
activities.fact: Fingernails grow about 3.5 millimetres a month, roughly twice as fast as toenails.

quiz.q: Why are manicure tools sterilised between clients?
quiz.explain: Sterilising tools kills germs, so infections cannot pass from one client to the next.

activities.scene: a student giving a classmate a neat manicure at a salon station with polish bottles
activities.place: in a clean, bright beauty therapy room

activities.name: Karate
activities.summary: Karate builds fitness, self-discipline and self-defence skills, with graded belts that reward steady progress.
activities.fact: Karate means “empty hand” in Japanese. It developed on the island of Okinawa.

quiz.q: What does the word “karate” mean?
quiz.explain: Kara means empty and te means hand.

activities.scene: a row of students in white karate uniforms performing a kata in unison
activities.place: in the school hall with mats on the floor

activities.name: Rugby
activities.summary: A fast, physical team game that builds fitness, courage and teamwork, coached with safe tackling technique.
activities.fact: A try in rugby union is worth 5 points, and the conversion kick after it adds 2 more.

quiz.q: How many points is a try worth in rugby union?
quiz.explain: A try scores 5 points; a successful conversion adds 2.

activities.scene: a rugby player running with the ball past a tackler, teammates in support
activities.place: on the school rugby field on a sunny afternoon

activities.name: Hockey
activities.summary: Field hockey sharpens speed, skill and teamwork, in a sport with a proud Zimbabwean history.
activities.fact: Zimbabwe’s women’s hockey team won gold at the 1980 Moscow Olympics, the country’s first Olympic medal.

quiz.q: In which year did Zimbabwe’s women’s hockey team win Olympic gold?
quiz.explain: The team won gold at the 1980 Moscow Olympic Games.

activities.scene: a hockey player sprinting with the ball on her stick, opponents chasing

activities.name: Basketball
activities.summary: Quick passing, sharp shooting and teamwork on court, building fitness, coordination and confidence.
activities.fact: Basketball was invented in 1891 by James Naismith, using two peach baskets as hoops.

quiz.q: How many players does each basketball team have on court?
quiz.explain: Each team has five players on court at a time.

activities.scene: a student leaping for a lay-up as teammates watch
activities.place: on an outdoor basketball court at the school

activities.name: Tennis
activities.summary: A lifelong sport that builds footwork, focus and fair play, from first rallies to competitive matches.
activities.fact: In tennis, “love” means zero, so a score of “15–love” means one player has a point and the other has none.

quiz.q: In tennis scoring, what comes after 15 and 30?
quiz.explain: The points go love, 15, 30, 40, then game.

activities.scene: a student hitting a forehand with a tennis racket, mid-swing

activities.name: Woodball
activities.summary: A precise, sociable sport where players strike a wooden ball through small gates, building focus, technique and patience.
activities.fact: Woodball was invented in Taiwan in 1990. Players hit a wooden ball with a mallet through small gates, a bit like golf.

quiz.q: Woodball is most similar to which sport?
quiz.explain: Like golf, woodball is played on a course, aiming for the fewest strikes.

activities.scene: a student lining up a woodball mallet behind the wooden ball, aiming at a small gate

activities.name: Volleyball
activities.summary: A fast team sport of quick reactions and teamwork, building agility, jumping power and communication.
activities.fact: Volleyball was invented in 1895 by William G. Morgan, who first called it “mintonette”.

quiz.q: How many players does a volleyball team have on court?
quiz.explain: Six players per team, who rotate positions during the game.

activities.scene: a student jumping to spike the ball over the net as a blocker rises

activities.name: Handball
activities.summary: A fast, high-scoring team game combining running, jumping, passing and throwing.
doing: Passing and catching on the move
activities.fact: In handball, a player may take only three steps while holding the ball before they must pass, shoot or bounce it.

quiz.q: How many players does a handball team have on court, including the goalkeeper?
quiz.explain: Six court players plus one goalkeeper: seven in all.

activities.scene: a student in mid-air making a jump shot towards the goal

activities.name: Softball
activities.summary: A bat-and-ball team sport that builds hand-eye coordination, speed and team spirit.
activities.fact: Softball began in Chicago in 1887, played indoors with a rolled-up boxing glove as the ball.

quiz.q: In softball, how is the ball pitched?
quiz.explain: Softball pitchers throw underarm.

activities.scene: a student batter swinging at a pitch, the catcher crouched behind

activities.name: Girls' Soccer / Football
activities.summary: Girls’ football builds skill, fitness and teamwork, in a sport where Zimbabwe’s women already compete on the world stage.
activities.fact: Zimbabwe’s women’s football team, the Mighty Warriors, played at the 2016 Rio Olympic Games.

quiz.q: How long is a full football match, not counting extra time?
quiz.explain: Two halves of 45 minutes make 90 minutes.

activities.scene: a girl dribbling the football past a defender, both focused on the ball

activities.name: Netball
activities.summary: A fast, skilful team game of quick passing and accurate shooting, and one of Zimbabwe’s most popular sports for girls.
activities.fact: Zimbabwe’s national netball team, the Gems, made their World Cup debut in 2019 and finished eighth.

quiz.q: How many players does a netball team have on court?
quiz.explain: Seven players, each with a position bib such as GS, GA or C.

activities.scene: a netball player jumping to shoot at the hoop while a defender reaches up

activities.name: Table Tennis
activities.summary: Fast rallies that sharpen reflexes, coordination and concentration, and a favourite after-school game.
activities.fact: A table-tennis ball weighs just 2.7 grams, yet top players can smash it at more than 100 km/h.

quiz.q: How many points do you need to win a game of table tennis?
quiz.explain: A game is played to 11 points, and you must win by two.

activities.scene: two students in a fast table-tennis rally, one leaning in for a forehand

activities.name: Chess
activities.summary: Chess trains patience, memory and strategic thinking, the same skills that help in maths and exams.
activities.fact: The knight is the only chess piece that can jump over other pieces.

quiz.q: How many squares are on a chessboard?
quiz.explain: Eight rows of eight squares: 64.

activities.scene: two students deep in thought over a chess game, one about to move a knight

activities.name: Darts
activities.summary: A game of focus and quick mental arithmetic: every throw is a sum.
activities.fact: On a standard dartboard the bullseye is 1.73 metres from the floor, and the 20 sits at the top.

quiz.q: How much is the bullseye (inner bull) worth in darts?
quiz.explain: The inner bull scores 50; the outer bull scores 25.

activities.scene: a student throwing a dart at a dartboard while friends keep score on a small board

activities.name: Quiz
activities.summary: Team quizzes on science, history, sport and current affairs that sharpen memory, general knowledge and teamwork.
activities.fact: Testing yourself is one of the best ways to remember what you learn. Researchers call it retrieval practice.

quiz.q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
quiz.explain: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.

activities.scene: a team of students huddled together, one raising a hand to answer a quiz question
activities.place: in a classroom set up for a quiz night

activities.name: Balloon Volleyball
activities.summary: A fun, fast indoor game that builds teamwork, coordination and plenty of laughter.
activities.fact: A balloon falls slowly because air resistance is large compared with its tiny weight, which gives everyone time to reach it.

quiz.q: What slows a falling balloon the most?
quiz.explain: Air resistance pushes up against the balloon’s large surface.

activities.scene: students laughing as they tap a big balloon over a low net
